scope: Existing mapped requirements, not a claim of complete or educator-approved curriculum. Working questions means at least one mapped competency has grade-eligible keyboard practice. Partial includes method/drawing requirements that cannot be fulfilled by final answers.

release.title: Ganita Prakash: Textbook of Mathematics for Grade 7, Part I and Part II — Grade 7 Mathematics (CBSE / NCERT)

chapters.title: A Peek Beyond the Point (Part 1, chapter 3)
Another Peek Beyond the Point (Part 2, chapter 4)
A Tale of Three Intersecting Lines (Part 1, chapter 7)

requirements.text: Explain place value as repeated groupings of ten (e.g. how many thousands make a lakh, how many lakhs make a crore).
Read, write and compare numbers up to crores in the Indian system and convert them to and from the international system (millions, billions).
requirements.reason: not every part is assessed: Converting from the international system back to the Indian system (millions to lakhs/crores) and billions are not assessed: ajmill only turns crores into millions, and ajcrore's pool has no million/billion items despite its stated limits.

requirements.text: Tell when an exact value is needed and when an approximate one is enough, and round large numbers sensibly.
Use patterns in products (e.g. multiplying by powers of ten) to calculate and estimate large products and to judge the size of large quantities.
requirements.reason: not every part is assessed: Judging the size of large quantities (e.g. how many days 1 lakh seconds is, or whether 1 crore of something is plausible) is not asked; only products with powers of ten and estimates of products are.

requirements.text: Write an arithmetic expression for a situation and evaluate it.
Identify the terms of an expression and evaluate expressions with brackets using the conventions for order of operations.
Compare or rewrite expressions without fully evaluating them by swapping and grouping terms and handling signs when removing brackets.
Represent tenths, hundredths and thousandths in decimal notation and state the place value of each digit.
Locate decimals on a number line and compare and order them.
Add and subtract decimals, including in measurement and money problems.
requirements.reason: not every part is assessed: Money word problems are not assessed: agrupee gives only bare rupee sums and differences (measurement problems are covered by agmeas).

requirements.text: Write measurements in larger units using decimals (e.g. cm to m, g to kg) and convert between them.
Multiply fractions and mixed numbers, and interpret the product with an area model.
Divide fractions and whole numbers using reciprocals.
Solve word problems that need multiplication or division of fractions.
Add and subtract integers fluently (revision of Grade 6).
Multiply integers using sign rules, explained through patterns or models.
Evaluate expressions and solve context problems that combine integer operations.
Find the highest common factor (HCF) of two or more numbers.
Solve word problems that need an HCF or an LCM, such as grouping or scheduling.
Find the least common multiple (LCM) of two or more numbers.
Explore properties linking HCF and LCM (e.g. HCF x LCM = product of two numbers) and use an efficient procedure to find the HCF.
Multiply decimals by whole numbers, by powers of ten and by other decimals.
Divide decimals by whole numbers, by powers of ten and by other decimals.
Estimate before calculating to check that decimal products and quotients are reasonable, and solve problems in context.
Use letters for unknown or varying quantities to write algebraic expressions for situations.
Evaluate algebraic expressions for given values of the letters.
Simplify algebraic expressions by collecting like terms, following the convention of leaving out the multiplication sign.
Describe patterns (e.g. in matchstick figures or calendars) with algebraic expressions and use them to reveal relationships.
Write a linear equation in one unknown to model a situation or puzzle.
Find and correct mistakes in worked solutions of equations.
Solve linear equations in one unknown systematically by doing the same operation to both sides, and check the solution.
Solve word problems by forming and solving a linear equation.
Use the facts that angles in a linear pair add to 180 degrees and that vertically opposite angles are equal to find unknown angles where two lines cross.
Identify perpendicular and parallel lines, and make them by paper folding.
Name the corresponding and alternate angles made by a transversal and use them to find unknown angles when the lines are parallel.
Use angle conditions to decide whether two lines are parallel and justify the decision.
Draw a line parallel to a given line through a given point using geometric tools.
Construct a triangle from three given side lengths and use the triangle inequality to decide whether such a triangle exists.
Construct a triangle from two sides and the included angle, or from two angles and a side.
Use the fact that the angles of a triangle add to 180 degrees to find unknown angles and to decide whether given angles can form a triangle.
Draw the altitudes of a triangle.
Classify triangles by their sides and by their angles.
Use the SSS, SAS, ASA/AAS and RHS conditions to decide whether two triangles are congruent.
Recognise congruent figures and match corresponding sides and angles of congruent triangles.
Use the equal-angle properties of isosceles and equilateral triangles to find unknown angles and justify them.
Decide which shapes can tile a flat surface without gaps or overlaps, using the angles that meet at a point.
Carry out the ruler-and-compass constructions in the chapter and explain why each one works.
Create and describe tiling patterns made from one or more shapes.
Tell statistical questions (answered by collecting varying data) apart from other questions and from statements.
Investigate a question with data and justify a conclusion from the evidence.
Calculate the mean and median of a data set and choose the more suitable representative value.
Choose and draw a suitable graph for a data set and read information from graphs.
Predict and justify whether a sum, difference or product is even or odd without calculating it.
Solve and reason about grid puzzles such as magic squares with given row, column and diagonal sums.
Generate Virahanka-Fibonacci numbers, link them to counting problems (e.g. rhythms of short and long beats), and explore their patterns.
requirements.reason: not every part is assessed: Exploring patterns in the Virahanka-Fibonacci numbers (e.g. sums of terms, which terms are even) is not asked: ahfib has a single form asking for a later term, and ahrhy covers only the counting link.

requirements.text: Work out the hidden digits in letter-coded addition or multiplication puzzles.

Check which properties (closure, commutative, associative, identity, distributive) hold for each integer operation, using counterexamples where a property fails.
Solve word problems that need several integer operations, such as temperature changes, depths or scores.
Recognise when two quantities vary inversely and solve problems about workers and time or speed and time.

Locate decimal numbers on a number line.
Apply the product, quotient, power-of-a-power and zero-exponent laws to simplify expressions.
Write repeated products in exponential form and evaluate powers, including expressing a number as a product of prime powers.
Find the unit digit of a large power using the repeating cycle of unit digits.
Determine the degree of a monomial or polynomial expression.
Round decimals to the nearest whole number, tenth or hundredth.
Add and subtract decimal numbers, including in money and measurement problems.
requirements.reason: not every part is assessed: Money word problems are not assessed: agrupee gives only bare rupee sums and differences (measurement problems are covered by agmeas).

requirements.text: Multiply decimals by whole numbers, by powers of 10 and by other decimals.
Divide decimals by whole numbers, by powers of 10 and by other decimals, and solve related word problems.
Convert between fractions, decimals and percentages.
Calculate a percentage of a quantity and express one quantity as a percentage of another in real-life situations such as marks, populations or discounts.

Identify the terms, coefficients and constants of an expression, and tell like terms from unlike terms.

Evaluate an algebraic expression for given values of its variables.
Form and solve simple linear equations in one variable from word problems.
Find the linear rule linking two quantities from a table of values and use it to predict new values.
Build Pascal's triangle and describe the number patterns in its rows and diagonals.
Use area models to multiply monomials and binomials.
Verify the identities for (a+b)^2, (a-b)^2 and (a+b)(a-b) with area diagrams and use them to expand expressions.
Factorise expressions that match a standard identity.
Solve simple one-variable inequations over whole numbers or integers and show the solution set on a number line.
Use adjacent angles, linear pairs and vertically opposite angles at intersecting lines to find unknown angles.
Identify the corresponding, alternate and co-interior angles formed by a transversal, and use them to find angles or test lines for parallelism.
Construct the perpendicular bisector of a line segment and the bisector of an angle with ruler and compass.
Construct special angles such as 60, 30, 90, 45 and 120 degrees with ruler and compass only.
Fit tetromino shapes together to tile or fill a given region.
Read a route map to describe paths with directions and choose the shortest or most suitable route.
Use the angle-sum property and the exterior-angle property to find unknown angles of triangles.
Identify corresponding parts of congruent figures and use the SSS, SAS, ASA and RHS criteria to decide whether two triangles are congruent.
Apply reflections, translations and rotations to figures and identify the symmetry each transformation produces.

requirements.text: Construct circles and concentric circles from given radii, or from a given ring width, using a compass.
Calculate the area and perimeter of a parallelogram from its base, height and sides, and find a missing dimension.
Calculate the area of a rhombus from its diagonals and use it to find an unknown diagonal.
Calculate the area of a trapezium from its parallel sides and height, including in field and plot problems.
Name the parts of a circle and relate radius and diameter.
Calculate the circumference of a circle and find the radius from a given circumference, including distance-by-wheel problems.

Find the area of rectangular and circular pathways by subtracting inner areas from outer areas.
Collect and organise data into tables.
Find the mode and median of ungrouped data and choose an appropriate representative value.
Calculate the arithmetic mean of a data set and interpret it as a representative value.
Read a flowchart that uses the standard symbols and trace it to find the output.

release.title: Mathematics: Textbook for Class X — Grade 10 Mathematics (CBSE / NCERT)

chapters.title: Pair of Linear Equations in Two Variables

requirements.text: Find the HCF and LCM of numbers from their prime factorisations, use HCF x LCM = product for two numbers, and solve word problems with them.
Use uniqueness of prime factorisation to justify number facts, e.g. that 6^n can never end in 0.
Express a natural number as a product of primes and state the Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic (uniqueness of prime factorisation).
Prove by contradiction that sqrt 2, sqrt 3 and sqrt 5 are irrational, using the fact that if a prime divides a^2 it divides a.
Prove that numbers such as 3 + 2 sqrt 5 or 1/sqrt 2 are irrational, given the irrationality of the surd.
Find the number of zeros of a polynomial from its graph by counting where it meets the x-axis.
Write a quadratic polynomial whose zeros have a given sum and product.
Find the zeros of a quadratic polynomial by factorising, and check the sum and product of zeros against the coefficients.
Evaluate symmetric expressions in the zeros (e.g. alpha^2 + beta^2, 1/alpha + 1/beta) without finding the zeros, and find unknown coefficients from conditions on the zeros.
Represent a situation as a pair of linear equations in two variables.
Solve a pair of linear equations graphically and interpret intersecting, parallel and coincident lines.
Decide from the coefficient ratios a1/a2, b1/b2, c1/c2 whether a pair has one, none or infinitely many solutions, and find parameter values for a given case.
Solve a pair of linear equations by substitution.
Solve a pair of linear equations by elimination.
Model and solve everyday problems (ages, money, speeds, digits, geometry) with a pair of linear equations and interpret the solution.
Recognise quadratic equations in standard form ax^2 + bx + c = 0 (a not 0) and form them from situations.
requirements.reason: Solve quadratic equations: missing relations; not every part is assessed: Forming a quadratic equation from a situation is never itself asked: auqwp says 'form a quadratic equation' but check only the final root, which can be found by trial; auqstd covers recognising and standard form only.

requirements.text: Solve quadratic equations with real roots using the quadratic formula.
Solve quadratic equations by factorisation (splitting the middle term).
Model everyday problems (areas, speeds, ages, numbers) with quadratic equations, solve them and reject solutions that do not fit the context.
Use the discriminant to decide the nature of roots and find parameter values for equal or real roots.
Derive and use the nth-term formula of an AP, including the nth term from the end and which term has a given value.
Decide whether a list is an AP and identify its first term and common difference.
Derive and use the formula for the sum of the first n terms of an AP.
Solve everyday problems (savings, instalments, arrangements) with AP terms and sums.
requirements.reason: not every part is assessed: Everyday problems (savings, instalments, arrangements) are not assessed: apn, auaps and auapk ask only for terms and sums of bare APs, with no context in any of their 3,360 problems.

requirements.text: Prove the Basic Proportionality Theorem: a line parallel to one side of a triangle divides the other two sides in the same ratio.
Use the BPT and its converse to find lengths and to show lines are parallel.
Explain when figures are similar versus congruent, with examples and counterexamples (e.g. polygons with equal angles but sides not in proportion).
Prove triangles similar and deduce relations between their sides, such as equal products of segments.
Apply the AA/AAA, SSS and SAS similarity criteria to find unknown sides and angles.
Use tangent properties to find lengths and angles and to prove results such as AB + CD = AD + BC for a quadrilateral circumscribing a circle.
Tell tangents, secants and non-intersecting lines apart and state how many tangents can be drawn from a point inside, on or outside a circle.
Prove that the tangent at any point of a circle is perpendicular to the radius through the point of contact.
Prove that the two tangents drawn from an external point to a circle are equal in length.
Calculate the area of a sector and the length of its arc from the radius and central angle.
Calculate the area of a segment of a circle for central angles of 60, 90 or 120 degrees.
Solve applied problems with sectors and segments, such as clock hands, wipers and designs.
Calculate the surface area of a solid made of two basic solids (cube, cuboid, cylinder, cone, sphere, hemisphere), deciding which faces stay exposed.
requirements.reason: not every part is assessed: combinations with a cuboid or a whole sphere are not asked (cube combinations are)

requirements.text: Model real objects (toys, tents, capsules, vessels) as combinations of solids and answer questions about material or capacity.
Calculate the volume of a solid made of two basic solids.
requirements.reason: not every part is assessed: combinations with a cuboid or a whole sphere are not asked (cube combinations are)

requirements.text: Calculate the mean of grouped data by the direct, assumed-mean and step-deviation methods.
Find a missing frequency from a given mean or median and interpret which measure of centre suits a situation.
Calculate the mode of grouped data from the modal class with the formula.
Calculate the median of grouped data using cumulative frequencies and the median formula.
Calculate theoretical (classical) probabilities for experiments with equally likely outcomes, such as coins, dice, cards and balls in bags.
Use the facts that P(E) + P(not E) = 1, that 0 <= P(E) <= 1, and that impossible and sure events have probabilities 0 and 1.
List the sample space of two-stage experiments (two coins, two dice) and find probabilities of events defined on it.
Use distances to test collinearity, classify triangles and quadrilaterals, and find points equidistant from given points.
Find the point dividing a segment internally in a given ratio, including the midpoint and points of trisection.
Calculate the distance between two points with the distance formula.
Find the ratio in which a point or an axis divides a segment, and unknown vertices (e.g. of a parallelogram) using the section formula.
Define the six trigonometric ratios of an acute angle in a right triangle and explain, using similarity, why they depend only on the angle.
Find the other trigonometric ratios of an angle from one given ratio.
Recall and justify the ratios of 30, 45 and 60 degrees (and the motivated values at 0 and 90), and evaluate expressions with them.
Prove sin^2 A + cos^2 A = 1 and the related identities with sec/tan and cosec/cot.
Prove simple trigonometric identities and simplify expressions using the basic identities.
Identify angles of elevation and depression and draw a labelled diagram for a heights-and-distances situation.
Find heights or distances with one right triangle and angles of 30, 45 or 60 degrees.
Solve heights-and-distances problems involving two right triangles (e.g. two observation points, an object seen from a height).

release.title: Mathematics, Standard Ten — Grade 10 Mathematics (Tamil Nadu State Board)

requirements.text: Form ordered pairs and Cartesian products of two or three sets and find the number of elements in a product.
Decide whether a relation is a function using arrow diagrams, ordered pairs, tables, rules and the vertical line test, and represent functions in these forms.
requirements.reason: not every part is assessed: Deciding from an arrow diagram is not assessed (aoisfn uses ordered pairs, tables, point plots with the vertical line test and rules; none of its 190 problems is an arrow diagram), and representing a function in these forms is asked only once, as an arrow diagram in wr:fn:one-one-onto (a).

requirements.text: Identify relations as subsets of a Cartesian product and state their domain, co-domain and range.
Classify functions as one-one, many-one, onto, into or bijective, and recognise constant, identity and real-valued functions.
requirements.reason: not every part is assessed: Recognising a real-valued function is never asked (one-one/many-one, onto/into, bijective, constant and identity are all in aofname/aqonto).

requirements.text: Form and evaluate compositions of functions and check whether composition is commutative or associative for given functions.
requirements.reason: Combine functions by sum, difference, product, quotient and composition: missing relations

requirements.text: Recognise and sketch graphs of linear, modulus, quadratic, cubic, reciprocal and constant functions.
Use congruence modulo n to find remainders, solve simple congruences and model cyclic situations such as clock times and weekdays.
Apply Euclid's division lemma and algorithm to find the HCF of integers and to prove statements about integer forms.
Use the fundamental theorem of arithmetic to factorise numbers, find HCF and LCM, and reason about divisibility and terminating decimals.
Find terms of sequences from general or recursive rules, and find nth terms, number of terms and conditions for arithmetic progressions.
Find the sum of the first n terms of an arithmetic series and solve related word problems.
requirements.reason: not every part is assessed: Word problems on arithmetic series are not assessed: auaps asks the sum of bare APs only, and wr:ap:derive-sum (c) is a bare number sum.

requirements.text: Find nth terms of geometric progressions, sums of finite and infinite geometric series, and solve related problems.
Evaluate sums of the first n natural numbers, odd numbers, squares and cubes using standard formulas.
requirements.reason: Sum special series of natural numbers: missing relations

requirements.text: Solve a system of three linear equations in three variables by elimination and recognise systems with no or infinitely many solutions.
requirements.reason: not every part is assessed: Solving by elimination is not seen: al3sys is answer-only and no written task asks for the elimination steps for three variables (almeth covers two variables only).

requirements.text: Find the GCD and LCM of polynomials and use the relation that their product equals the product of the two polynomials.
Reduce rational expressions to lowest terms, state excluded values, and multiply, divide, add and subtract rational expressions.
Find the square root of a perfect-square polynomial by factorisation and by the long-division method.
Solve quadratic equations by factorisation, completing the square and the formula, and apply them to word problems.

Construct a triangle given its base, vertical angle and either the median, the altitude, or the point where the vertical-angle bisector meets the base.
Prove the Pythagoras theorem and its converse and apply them, including Pythagorean triples.

requirements.text: Apply tangent properties (radius–tangent perpendicularity, equal tangents from an external point, alternate segment theorem, common tangents) to find lengths and angles.

Construct a tangent at a point on a circle and a pair of tangents from an external point, and measure their lengths.

Calculate curved and total surface areas of solid and hollow cylinders.
Calculate surface area and volume of a frustum of a cone.
Find surface areas and volumes of solids formed by combining cylinders, cones, spheres and hemispheres.
Solve problems where a solid is melted or recast into another shape using conservation of volume.
Compute variance and standard deviation for raw, ungrouped and grouped data by direct, mean, assumed-mean and step-deviation methods.
